meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes, and the first thing I want to know is who decided Owen gets a zero, and why I found out from my son instead of from you.

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.

Forty minutes in a classroom with no book against a weekend at home with the play open in front of him. Of course one has quotations and fewer comma splices; that's called revising. Show me both pieces, and then answer my question: who decided on the zero before anyone called me?
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.

Then you gave him a zero on the strength of something you've just taken off the table. Show me the version history, with the dates and times on it. And you still haven't told me why my son learned about this from his phone.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero withdrawn, an apology, an explanation of why I was not contacted before the mark was entered, and to see the version history and both pieces of Owen's writing you described. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, having agreed to nothing, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, an explanation of why she wasn't called first, and to see your documents; the fair outcome would be a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and the meeting ended before you got there.
What moved her: nothing yet, because your comparison with the September 24 in-class writing was specific and dated, but you described it instead of putting it in front of her.
What cost ground: you never answered why the zero went in before anyone called her, and leaving her procedural question open twice kept her in attack mode.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near that night, since you mentioned the version history but showed no times; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: open with one sentence owning that the zero went into the gradebook before you called her, then put the version history with its times in front of her rather than telling her what it shows.
